title: Largest Combination With Bitwise AND Greater Than Zero
spaceBreakdown:
- No containers or arrays allocated
- No recursion
- Only a fixed set of scalar variables (ans, cnt, loop counters) → O(1)
approach: For a bitwise AND to be greater than zero, at least one bit position must be 1 in every element of the combination. So for each of the 24 bit positions (since candidates[i] ≤ 10^7 < 2^24), count how many candidates have that bit set. The maximum count across all bit positions is the answer, because all candidates sharing a common set bit can be combined and their AND will have that bit as 1.
hints: For the bitwise AND of a group of numbers to be positive, what must be true about at least one bit position across every number in that group? The values are at most 10^7, which fits in 24 bits.
For each of the 24 bit positions, count how many candidates have that bit set; the answer is the maximum such count. Example: bit 4 (value 16) is set in 16, 17, 62, 24 - that's 4 candidates.

**Single element** - n = 1, but the value is positive so at least one bit is set.
`Input: [7]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: only updating `ans` when `cnt > 1` → returns 0

**All distinct powers of two** - each bit position is set in exactly one element.
`Input: [1,2,4,8,16]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: returning the sum of all bit counts instead of the maximum → returns 5

**Value uses the highest bit** - 2^23 = 8388608 ≤ 10^7, so bit 23 is needed.
`Input: [8388608]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: looping bits 0..22 (only 23 iterations) → returns 0

**All elements equal** - every bit set in one element is set in all of them.
`Input: [8,8,8]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: deduplicating candidates into a set before counting → returns 1

followUps.q: What if candidates[i] can be up to 10^18?
followUps.a: Increase the bit range from 24 to 60. The algorithm is unchanged - iterate over 60 bit positions instead of 24. TC remains O(n) with a larger constant, SC stays O(1).

followUps.q: What if you must return the actual combination instead of just its size?
followUps.a: After finding the bit position with the maximum count, do a second pass collecting every candidate with that bit set. TC stays O(n), SC becomes O(n) to store the output list.

followUps.q: What if the input arrives as an unbounded stream and cannot be stored?
followUps.a: Maintain 24 running counters, one per bit position. For each incoming number, increment every counter whose bit is set, and track the running maximum counter. TC is O(24) per element, SC is O(24) = O(1).
